entities.summary:
Antoine-François, comte Andréossy was a Franco-Italian nobleman who served as a French Army artillery general, diplomat, and parliamentarian.

Born in Castelnaudary, France on March 6, 1761, Andréossy rose through the ranks of the French military, becoming a respected artillery commander during the French Revolutionary Wars.

As a diplomat, Andréossy played a key role in shaping French foreign policy, particularly in regards to Italy and the Mediterranean region.

He was also a prominent figure in the French parliament, advocating for reforms and modernization of the French military.

Andréossy's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the modern French state and contributed to the development of the French artillery corps.

In his later years, Andréossy became increasingly disillusioned with the French government's handling of the Italian wars, leading him to eventually retire from public life.

Today, Andréossy is remembered as a skilled military leader, astute diplomat, and devoted public servant who played a significant role in shaping the course of European history.
